Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-07-01", "authors": [{"authorId": "2151727855", "name": "Man Ling"}, {"authorId": "72541432", "name": "Xian-Chuan Wang"}, {"authorId": "2144217423", "name": "Xiu-Ming Chen"}], "abstract": "This paper presents a robust image hashing algorithm for copy detection that synergistically integrates Graph-Based Visual Saliency (GBVS) with Locality Preserving Projections (LPP). Unlike conventional pipelines that treat saliency detection and feature extraction as independent stages, the proposed framework employs the GBVS saliency map as a spatial attention mask to modulate Gabor-based texture features. This ensures that perceptually significant regions dominate the manifold structure preservation process. The weighted features are then projected via LPP to produce compact hash vectors that respect the local topology of the visual content. Comprehensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a True Positive Rate (TPR) of 99.84% at threshold T = 0.98 in robustness evaluation under various content-preserving attacks, an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.994 in discriminability evaluation, and an F1-Score of 0.984 in copy detection benchmarks. Systematic parameter sensitivity analysis and failure boundary evaluation further validate the algorithm\u2019s stability. Comparisons with representative traditional and deep learning-based hashing methods confirm that the proposed approach attains a superior balance between robustness, discriminability, and computational efficiency, particularly in resource-constrained scenarios."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "e4d171a72495d374240c2a0d5aa17ba100d07bf7", "externalIds": {"DOI": "10.1117/1.JEI.35.3.033024", "CorpusId": 289518135}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/e4d171a72495d374240c2a0d5aa17ba100d07bf7", "title": "Optimizing the number of neurons in the final hash layer of an image retrieval architecture using the Boruta\u2013Shap algorithm to achieve feature space compression and enhanced feature discriminability", "venue": "Journal of Electronic Imaging (JEI)", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": null, "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1117/1.JEI.35.3.033024?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.1117/1.JEI.35.3.033024, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-05-01", "authors": [{"authorId": "2183571051", "name": "Fatemeh Taheri"}, {"authorId": "2291821484", "name": "Kambiz Rahbar"}], "abstract": "Abstract. Hashing methods in image classification and retrieval convert high-dimensional feature vectors into compact codes, improving storage efficiency and search speed. Learnable hashing improves class separation by minimizing intraclass and maximizing interclass distances but faces challenges. Most approaches maintain similarity between feature vectors and hash codes through extensive training and complex loss functions. In transfer learning, generating distinctive hash codes can lead to model overfitting due to the limited number of target domain samples. To address this, a common approach is to use features from the fully connected layer as the hash unit. In hashing-based methods, the presence of irrelevant or unimportant neurons in the output layer can negatively affect similarity computation and the retrieval of relevant samples. Conversely, limiting the number of neurons in this layer reduces the complexity of the hash unit, resulting in a lightweight architecture that enables model training with fewer samples. However, excessive compression of hash codes due to aggressive neuron reduction may degrade model performance. We investigate the optimal selection of the number of neurons in the output layer of the hash unit by exploring the trade-off between hash code compression and retrieval performance using the Boruta\u2013Shap algorithm. The results demonstrate that the Euclidean distance becomes more discriminative as the number of neurons in the hash unit is reduced, thereby improving the retrieval of images similar to the query. Experimental results show that reducing the number of neurons from 1920 to 698 (63% reduction) improves retrieval accuracy on CIFAR-10. Furthermore, quantitative analysis indicates that the average Euclidean distance between query images and retrieved samples is reduced by up to 44% (from 9.16 to 5.21), whereas the average cosine similarity increases by up to 8% (from 0.72 to 0.78) compared with using a fully sized hashing layer."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "1ae3df841c8811d9e1a8b87c5c46e210521a6758", "externalIds": {"DBLP": "journals/frai/Tarawneh25", "PubMedCentral": "12929465", "DOI": "10.3389/frai.2025.1690830", "CorpusId": 285530588, "PubMed": "41743262"}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/1ae3df841c8811d9e1a8b87c5c46e210521a6758", "title": "HasLoss: a novel Hassanat distance-based loss functions for binary classification", "venue": "Frontiers Artif. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-02-10", "authors": [{"authorId": "144134300", "name": "Ahmad S. Tarawneh"}], "abstract": "Introduction Loss functions play a critical role in machine learning, particularly in training neural networks for classification tasks. In this work, we establish a theoretical framework for distance-based loss functions by adapting the Hassanat distance for binary classification. Methods Through gradient analysis, we prove that Hassanat losses exhibit bounded gradients with finite Lipschitz constants, providing convergence guarantees and robustness to outliers. We formulate six variants with different error sensitivities and validate these theoretical properties empirically. Their effectiveness is evaluated on synthetic datasets and nine real-world datasets, ranging from a few hundred to nearly 48,000 samples, under controlled experimental conditions. A comprehensive comparison is conducted against widely used loss functions, including Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE), Focal Loss, Mean Squared Error (MSE), and L1 Loss. Results Results show that the proposed Hassanat-based losses achieve competitive performance across evaluation metrics, with comparable or slightly improved results in calibration, convergence speed (in terms of epochs), precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC on several datasets, while exhibiting notable robustness to outliers and noise. The estimated Floating Point Operations (FLOPs) shows that the wall-clock time difference is due to implementation gap, not algorithmic. Importantly, Cohen's d effect size and confidence interval analyses shows that some of the proposed variants introduce a larger practical effect size than popular loss functions such as BCE. Discussion This work establishes both theoretical foundations and empirical validation for distance-based loss functions. The bounded gradient framework with finite Lipschitz constants provides principled optimization guarantees while explaining observed robustness and convergence behavior. This foundation enables systematic development of robust loss functions tailored to specific application requirements."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "d55754e4013c7b212f9d01aa99a4bbc8987ee79d", "externalIds": {"DBLP": "conf/sibgrapi/SilvaFSPBFAPSRA25", "DOI": "10.1109/SIBGRAPI67909.2025.11223501", "CorpusId": 282943805}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/d55754e4013c7b212f9d01aa99a4bbc8987ee79d", "title": "A Deep Metric Learning Approach for Content Based Image Retrieval in Rock Tomography: A Triplet Loss Study", "venue": "SIBGRAPI Conference on Graphics, Patterns and Images", "year": 2025, "citationCount": 2, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": "CLOSED", "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1109/SIBGRAPI67909.2025.11223501?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.1109/SIBGRAPI67909.2025.11223501, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Albuquerque"}], "abstract": "The automatic analysis of images in rock tomography datasets still is an unexplored task despite its high relevance in geological studies and characterization of materials. Traditional Content-Based Image Retrieval (CBIR) methods face difficulties when dealing with the structural complexity of these images while approaches based on deep learning still lack research specifically at this domain. In this paper we propose a CBIR approach using Deep Metric Learning with Triplet Loss function and different convolutional backbones. The results on the sandstone samples dataset has shown superior performance than the method found in the literature. The highlight was the DenseNet121 architecture, which obtained $99.23 \\% \\pm 0.14$ of F1-Score and $99.09\\% \\pm 0.16$ of mAP@10. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2025-06-01", "authors": [{"authorId": "2336309800", "name": "Rajath Arakere Narayanaswamy"}, {"authorId": "2336304396", "name": "Vidyalakshmi Krishne Gowda"}], "abstract": "Content-based image retrieval (CBIR) is an important research area that focuses on emerging techniques for handling large image collections and enabling efficient retrieval. The main challenge of image retrieval is to extract relevant feature vectors for image description. Therefore, visual geometric group 19 (VGG19) with Jaccard is proposed in this research for CBIR. The VGG19 allows to capture of hierarchical features, and it is appropriate for texture and fine detail characteristics. It enables to production of robust and discriminative feature representations because of numerous convolutional layers. The Jaccard is utilized as a similarity measure among feature vectors by comparing the union and intersection of feature sets. It is helpful to manage sparse and higher-dimensional data that provides a fast and accurate image retrieval process. The Caltech 256 and Corel 1K datasets are considered and it is preprocessed by image resizing and normalization. The raw images are resized to ensure dataset similarity and normalized into the range of 0 and 1. The metrics such as recall, f-measure, and average precision are used to calculate the VGG19-Jaccard performance. The VGG19-Jaccard achieves average precision of 99.0 and 99.8% for Caltech 256 and Corel 1K datasets compared to the two-stage CBIR technique."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "c2d83e40881b500ee66eb8871f0d7cbf8bdefe8a", "externalIds": {"DOI": "10.19101/ijatee.2024.111101498", "CorpusId": 277476646}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/c2d83e40881b500ee66eb8871f0d7cbf8bdefe8a", "title": "Breast cancer survival rate prediction using multimodal deep learning with multigenetic features", "venue": "International Journal of Advanced Technology and Engineering Exploration", "year": 2025, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "https://accentsjournals.org/PaperDirectory/Journal/IJATEE/2025/3/9.pdf", "status": "GOLD", "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.19101/ijatee.2024.111101498?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.19101/ijatee.2024.111101498, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. This research utilized three genetic expression profiles\u2014gene expression, deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) methylation, and micro ribonucleic acid (miRNA) expression\u2014to deepen the understanding of breast cancer biology and contribute to the development of a reliable survival rate prediction model. During the preprocessing phase, principal component analysis (PCA) was applied to reduce the dimensionality of each dataset before computing consensus features across the three omics datasets. By integrating these datasets with the consensus features, the model's ability to uncover deep connections within the data was significantly improved. The proposed multimodal deep learning multigenetic features (MDL-MG) architecture incorporates a custom attention mechanism (CAM), bidirectional long short-term memory (BLSTM), and convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Additionally, the model was optimized to handle contrastive loss by extracting distinguishing features using a Siamese network (SN) architecture with a Euclidean distance metric. To assess the effectiveness of this approach, various evaluation metrics were applied to the cancer genome atlas (TCGA-BREAST) dataset. The model achieved 100% accuracy and demonstrated improvements in recall (16.2%), area under the curve (AUC) (29.3%), and precision (10.4%) while reducing complexity. Shukla"}, {"authorId": "66072258", "name": "Partap Singh"}], "abstract": "Content-Based Image Retrieval (CBIR) has become an essential component in a wide range of vision-driven applications, where the objective is to retrieve semantically similar images from large-scale repositories based on visual content. In this work, we propose an enhanced hybrid feature extraction framework that combines ConvNeXt and EfficientNet for richer representation learning. Unlike conventional single-model approaches, our method concatenates the layer embeddings from the two networks, enabling a more comprehensive capture of local texture descriptors and global semantic abstractions. To rigorously assess similarity, we incorporate a broad spectrum of distance measures, including Cosine, Euclidean, Manhattan, Chebyshev, Minkowski, and Canberra. Experiments are conducted on three diverse and widely used benchmark datasets: Corel-1K, Corel-10K, and Caltech-101. The proposed dual-branch feature fusion consistently surpasses the individual backbone models and baseline methods across multiple evaluation metrics. Specifically, the framework achieves a precision of 99.17% on Corel-1K, 90.74% on Corel-10K, and 92.24% on Caltech-101, along with strong recall, F1-score, and accuracy performance across all distance measures. These results validate the robustness of the hybrid representation in capturing inter-class variability and intra-class similarity. This study contributes a scalable, architecture-agnostic paradigm for deep feature fusion in CBIR and highlights the potential of enriched hybrid embeddings for improving visual search in large-scale image databases."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "08dc9ba5d476836d3e743512a0ade4ca9d7e257a", "externalIds": {"DOI": "10.12720/jait.17.8.1477-1497", "CorpusId": 291153006}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/08dc9ba5d476836d3e743512a0ade4ca9d7e257a", "title": "Deep Image Retrieval Using Optimizer-aware Convolutional Neural Network with Adaptive Adam-AMSGrad Fusion", "venue": "Journal of Advances in Information Technology", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "https://www.jait.us/articles/2026/JAIT-V17N8-1477.pdf", "status": "GOLD", "license": "CCBY", "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.12720/jait.17.8.1477-1497?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.12720/jait.17.8.1477-1497, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content.
